seo_title: Cost of Living in Porto 2026: Visa, Prices, Reviews | Relocost
seo_description: How much does it cost to live in Porto per month, do Russians need a visa, work, rent and reviews from those who relocated. A realistic moving budget in the Relocost calculator.
intro_text: An Atlantic alternative to Lisbon — roughly 15% cheaper, with a mild climate and a historic setting. Relocation goes through the D7/D8 visas and requires proven income and patience with AIMA bureaucracy.
pros: A mild Atlantic climate: no heat and no frost
About 15% cheaper than Lisbon for the same quality of life
A historic setting, the ocean and the Douro Valley nearby
A growing community of remote workers and good coworkings
Clear visa routes — D7/D8 into the Schengen area
cons: A Schengen visa and long AIMA bureaucracy — appointments take months to get
Proven income required: D7 from €920, D8 from ~€3,500 per month
The Portuguese language and a strict check on the source of funds
Frequent rain and damp in winter, with weak heating
Rents have risen, and good apartments are snapped up quickly

visa_steps.title: D7 or D8 visa
visa_steps.description: D7 — for passive income from €920/month, D8 — for remote workers from ~€3,500/month. Submitted at the consulate.

visa_steps.title: NIF and account
visa_steps.description: A NIF tax number and an account at a Portuguese bank (Millennium BCP, ActivoBank) — the basic step.

visa_steps.title: Rental with a contract
visa_steps.description: You need a registered rental contract as proof of address.

visa_steps.title: Entry and AIMA
visa_steps.description: After the visa — an AIMA appointment for biometrics and the residency card; the wait can drag on for months.

visa_steps.title: Residency and renewal
visa_steps.description: The first residency is for 2 years, then a renewal; after 5 years — a path to permanent residency and citizenship.

faq.question: Do Russian citizens need a visa for Porto?
faq.answer: Yes, Portugal is in the Schengen area. For relocation you apply for a national D7 (passive income) or D8 (remote work) visa.

faq.question: How much money do you need for a Porto visa?
faq.answer: D7 — proven income from €920 a month, D8 (digital nomad) — from ~€3,500 a month for one person.

faq.question: Is Porto cheaper than Lisbon?
faq.answer: Yes, rent and living costs in Porto are roughly 15% lower than in the capital, at a comparable level.

faq.question: What is the climate like in Porto?
faq.answer: Atlantic and mild: no heat and no frost, but with lots of rain and damp in winter.

faq.question: Can I pay with a Russian card in Porto?
faq.answer: No, Russian cards don't work. You need an account and card from a local bank, which require a NIF.

faq.question: How do I open an account in Porto?
faq.answer: Through a NIF (tax number) at Millennium BCP or ActivoBank; a lawyer-intermediary often helps.

reviews.text: We did the D8 for the two of us: our income was enough, but we waited half a year for an AIMA appointment. Porto is quiet and beautiful, the ocean is 20 minutes away, and the rain is the price of the climate.
I did the D7 based on rental income from an apartment in Russia. The bureaucracy wears you down, but after residency — the whole Schengen area and a calm life by the water.
